hypothesis.statement: In Li₃PX₄ orthothiophosphates and orthophosphates, the Li migration barrier depends mainly on the anion sublattice, not on how the PX₄ tetrahedra are arranged. Swapping O²⁻ for S²⁻ in a fixed framework lowers the barrier substantially, because S²⁻ is more polarizable and screens the moving Li⁺ better at the saddle point, and because it gives a larger, softer lattice with wider Li–Li bottlenecks. The same substitution raises energy above hull, because the oxide is the thermodynamically stronger lattice.
hypothesis.rationale: The notebook is empty, so this is a prior, not a result. The goal asks for a low barrier and stability together, and the usual expectation is that these pull against each other through the anion. If that trade-off is real and anion-driven, later rounds should be organized around anion chemistry. If framework topology matters as much or more, later rounds should search over structure types instead. The test is cheap: Li₃PO₄ and Li₃PS₄ each have two polymorphs forming two isostructural O/S pairs (Pmn2₁ and Pnma), giving a 2×2 anion × framework design that separates the two effects directly. Limits: energy above hull is a proxy for bulk thermodynamic stability, not stability against Li metal. A phase can sit on the hull and still be reduced by Li, as thiophosphates can be toward Li₂S and Li₃P. Reaction energy with Li (or reduction potential) is not a campaign objective, so no Li-metal compatibility will be claimed for any candidate. Barriers come from perfect-crystal, picosecond-scale calculations and say nothing about grain-boundary transport, interphase growth, or real conductivity.
hypothesis.prediction: In both the Pmn2₁ pair and the Pnma pair, the sulfide migration barrier will be at least 0.15 eV lower than the oxide barrier. The anion effect (mean of the two O→S barrier drops) will exceed the framework effect (Pmn2₁ vs Pnma barrier difference at fixed anion, averaged over O and S). Energy above hull (eV/atom) will be higher for the sulfide than for the oxide in each pair.
hypothesis.falsification_criterion: The claim is refuted if, in either isostructural pair, the sulfide barrier is not at least 0.15 eV below the oxide barrier, or if the framework effect is as large as or larger than the anion effect. Separately, if the sulfide energy above hull is equal to or lower than the oxide's in both pairs, the trade-off premise is refuted independently. A pair comparison counts only if both members used the same hopping mechanism (vacancy vs interstitial) and comparable supercell treatment; a mismatched pair is logged as insufficient data and counts as neither support nor refutation. No OOD-flagged barrier may decide the outcome by itself.

batch_plan.strategy: A 2×2 anion × framework design matched by space group, not polymorph label: Li₃PO₄ Pmn2₁ (β), Li₃PS₄ Pmn2₁ (γ), Li₃PO₄ Pnma (γ), Li₃PS₄ Pnma (β). Li₃N P6/mmm is added as a reference baseline on both axes and is not part of the falsification test.

vetoes.reason: Li3N is not a Li3PX4 compound, has no PX4 tetrahedra and no oxide or sulfide analogue in this batch, so it cannot enter either pair, the anion effect or the framework effect of h1. It is a known Li conductor and belongs in its own branch, not this round.

LiN3 is an azide with an N3- molecular anion and covalent N-N bonding, not an orthophosphate or thiophosphate, so it cannot inform h1. Whether the model treats the azide anion reliably is a separate open question and not the basis of this veto.
Li4P2O7 is a pyrophosphate built from corner-sharing P2O7 units, not isolated PO4 tetrahedra, so it is outside the Li3PX4 family. No Li4P2S7 partner is offered, so it cannot form an anion pair.

body.commentary:
Approved: c-mp-13725 (Li3PO4) and c-mp-985583 (Li3PS4), both conditionally. They are the only Li3PX4 candidates and the only ones that can inform h1. Chemistry checks out: P5+ is tetrahedral, Li+ is charge-balanced, and both are retrieved database entries. No duplicates among the five ids.

Condition on the approval: the notebook records only MP ids, not space groups. h1 counts a pair only if both members share a framework (Pmn21 with Pmn21, or Pnma with Pnma). Confirm this from the retrieved structures before counting the two as a pair. If the frameworks differ, the barrier comparison is insufficient data under h1's own rules.

What this batch can test: the prediction needs four structures, Li3PO4 and Li3PS4 in each of Pmn21 and Pnma. This batch supplies at most two, and only if the space-group check passes.
- Framework effect: cannot be computed, because no anion has both frameworks here. The clause "anion effect exceeds framework effect" is insufficient data.
- Barrier clause: at most one pair can be evaluated. A sulfide barrier not at least 0.15 eV below the oxide in that pair would refute h1, since the clause reads "in either pair". A pass is partial support only.
- Energy-above-hull trade-off: refutation requires the sulfide to be equal or lower in both pairs, so one pair can neither refute nor confirm it.
The generator should add the other-framework Li3PO4 and Li3PS4 entries next round. Without them, h1 cannot reach a verdict.

Notes for the Analyst:
- Mechanism and supercell: stoichiometric Li3PX4 has no intrinsic carrier, so each barrier needs an introduced vacancy or interstitial. Check that both pair members used the same mechanism and a comparable supercell size and defect concentration. If they did not, log the pair as insufficient data.
- Upper bound: an NEB-type barrier covers only the hop computed. Unless several distinct hops were sampled, read each barrier as an upper bound on the lowest Li barrier. A failure to reach 0.15 eV could come from sampling a non-optimal sulfide hop, so check how many hops were computed before calling a refutation.
- Scope: these are 0 K single-hop barriers in supercells of at most a few hundred atoms. They are not conductivities or transport activation energies, and they say nothing about grain boundaries, defect formation energy or long-time diffusion.
- Disorder: experimental Pnma Li3PS4 has partially occupied Li sites, so any database entry is an ordered approximant. That is a structure type the method does not treat faithfully, so treat it as OOD. Whether this applies to c-mp-985583 depends on its space group, which is not in the notebook.
- Energy above hull is a weak proxy. It measures decomposition within the compound's own chemical system, not reduction by Li metal. The measurement that would actually test anode stability is missing: the reaction energy with Li, or phase stability at the Li-metal chemical potential. Report it as hull distance only.
- The oxide is referenced to the Li-P-O hull and the sulfide to the Li-P-S hull. A higher sulfide value is testable against the h1 clause as written, but it does not test the stated mechanism ("oxide is the stronger lattice").
- OOD: no measurements exist yet. An OOD-flagged barrier in a pair cannot decide h1 alone and counts only as weak evidence.

body.reasoning: The only comparison available, c-mp-13725 (Li3PO4) vs c-mp-985583 (Li3PS4), does not meet h1's own rules for counting as a pair. Isostructurality is unconfirmed because the notebook records no space groups. The supercells imply parent cells of 16 atoms (127+1 sites in 2x2x2) and 32 atoms (63+1 sites in 2x1x1). That is consistent with different frameworks but does not prove it. Both runs used a vacancy mechanism, but supercell treatment is not comparable: 1 vacancy per 48 Li sites in the oxide against 1 per 24 in the sulfide. The pair is therefore logged as insufficient data. The barrier clause cannot be scored. For the record, the uncounted gap is 0.051 eV, about a third of the 0.15 eV threshold, so it points toward refutation. Only one hop was computed per structure, so each barrier is an upper bound, and no eV error bar exists to say whether 0.051 eV is resolved. The framework clause is insufficient data because no anion was computed in both frameworks. The hull trade-off clause refutes only if the sulfide is equal or lower in both pairs, so one pair cannot trigger it. The MACE ordering (sulfide lower) is within MACE's +0.015 eV/atom offset from DFT, uses different chemical systems, and both DFT hull distances are 0, so the two are indistinguishable from on-hull. No measurement carries an OOD flag, but c-mp-985583 may be an ordered approximant of a partially occupied phase; its space group is unknown. Neither hull value tests stability against Li metal. Settling h1 needs the space groups of both compounds, the other-framework partners, and barriers for all four structures at matched vacancy concentration with every symmetry-distinct hop sampled.

heuristics.text: Compute both members of any comparison pair at the same number of Li sites per vacancy, or converge each barrier with supercell size; finite-size image interaction otherwise disqualifies the pair.
Sample every symmetry-distinct Li hop and score the lowest percolating path; a single NEB hop is an upper bound and cannot refute a lower-barrier claim.

Record the space group and Z of every candidate at retrieval and refuse to pair candidates with unconfirmed frameworks; treat a mismatch in parent-cell atom count as a red flag before computing barriers.
Do not rank stability on MACE hull differences below about 0.015 eV/atom in this family.
Add the reaction energy with Li metal as a scored measurement; a hull distance within the compound's own chemical system cannot speak to anode stability.
Prioritise a clean, matched rerun of the Li3PO4/Li3PS4 pair over new chemistry; the uncounted 0.051 eV gap suggests refutation is the likely outcome and it is cheap to confirm.

body.reasoning:
Continue with a matched rerun of the same Li3PO4 / Li3PS4 pair (c-mp-13725 / c-mp-985583). The trade-off clause is re-scored on reaction energy with Li metal instead of hull distance.

Why h1 was inconclusive: it failed on setup, not physics. The vacancy concentration was mismatched (1 per 24 Li sites for the sulfide vs 1 per 48 for the oxide). Only one hop was computed per structure. Frameworks were unconfirmed (parent cells of 16 and 32 atoms, no space groups recorded). No anode-stability measurement was on record.

What round 1 established: neither margin is resolved. The sulfide barrier, 0.275 eV, is 0.051 eV below the oxide's 0.326 eV. Both are single-hop upper bounds with no eV error bar. The MACE hull values, 0.0014 vs 0.0092 eV/atom, differ by 0.0078 eV/atom, which is below the 0.015 eV/atom ranking resolution. The two hulls come from different chemical systems, and MP DFT puts both compounds at 0. The frontier scalar 1.000 on c-mp-985583 therefore means not yet distinguished from Li3PO4. Nothing on record measures stability against Li metal. The band gap proxy (5.818 vs 2.81 eV, confidence 0.60) is ordinal only.

Round 2 specification:
(1) Log space group and Z for both compounds before any barrier. If the frameworks differ, log the result as an anion-plus-framework comparison.
(2) Match 1 vacancy per 48 Li sites, using a 2x2x1 sulfide supercell (128 sites). Run each compound at a second supercell size; the change in barrier is the finite-size error bar.
(3) Compute every symmetry-distinct hop and score the lowest barrier on a percolating path.
(4) Compute the reaction energy with Li metal on the MACE scale, with a DFT cross-check where MP has the competing phases.
(5) Include other-framework polymorphs only if they come with a confirmed space group. Otherwise drop the framework clause.

Pre-registered reading:
The barrier clause is refuted if the matched, all-hop sulfide barrier is not at least 0.15 eV below the oxide's, with the finite-size error bar taken into account.
The trade-off clause is supported if the sulfide's Li-metal reaction energy is more favourable (more negative) than the oxide's. It is refuted if it is equal or less favourable.
If the barrier advantage collapses and the oxide is the more Li-stable member, the frontier moves to Li3PO4.

Round 3 is held in reserve, not committed. Li3N (c-mp-2251) remains a candidate for a separate line, but nothing about its barrier or Li stability is on record, so it gets no ranking now.

No branch: with two rounds left, a branch would spend both and leave no round to act on the outcome.

hypothesis.statement: In Li3PX4 (X = O, S), the barrier for vacancy-mediated Li migration is set mainly by the anion: S2- is more polarizable and screens the Li+ at the saddle point, and the larger S lattice gives wider Li-Li bottlenecks. The arrangement of the PX4 tetrahedra (the framework) is a secondary effect, so swapping O for S at a fixed framework lowers the lowest percolating barrier by more than changing the framework at a fixed anion does. This is h1's barrier claim narrowed to a design that can score it. The hull trade-off clause is dropped, because a within-system hull distance cannot speak to anode stability and MACE hull differences below 0.015 eV/atom must not be ranked.
hypothesis.rationale: h1 was inconclusive, not refuted. The only barrier evidence is 0.326 eV for c-mp-13725 (Li3PO4) and 0.275 eV for c-mp-985583 (Li3PS4), a 0.051 eV gap. That gap has three problems. The vacancy concentrations differ (1 per 48 Li sites vs 1 per 24). Each barrier comes from a single hop. The frameworks are probably different (implied parent cells of 16 atoms, Z = 2, and 32 atoms, Z = 4, with no space group recorded). A single hop bounds only the lowest hop, not necessarily the percolating barrier, so neither number on record is a percolating-path barrier. A clean rerun alone cannot settle the claim if the compounds are not isostructural, so the batch adds the two crossed partners needed to hold the framework fixed. I expect refutation: the 0.051 eV gap is about a third of the threshold, and nothing in the notebook suggests matching concentration or sampling more hops would widen it by roughly 0.1 eV. I am not confident in that direction, because hop sampling can move either barrier either way. A refutation would mean framework and Li-site topology control the barrier more than anion chemistry in this family. Later rounds should then select on framework, and the vetoed Li3N line becomes a stronger candidate for its own branch. If both matched pairs show the sulfide at least 0.15 eV lower with a smaller framework effect, I will accept the anion as the main lever, and stability against Li metal becomes the open question, which h2 does not test.
hypothesis.prediction: Barriers are the lowest percolating vacancy-path barrier (MACE-MP-0) at matched vacancy concentration. The claim holds if all three are true. (1) In framework A (the framework of c-mp-13725), the sulfide barrier is at least 0.15 eV below the oxide's. (2) In framework B (the framework of c-mp-985583), the sulfide barrier is at least 0.15 eV below the oxide's. (3) For each anion, |barrier(A) - barrier(B)| is smaller than the smaller of the two anion-swap differences.
hypothesis.falsification_criterion: h2 is refuted by either of two outcomes in a pair that counts. First, in any valid fixed-framework pair, the sulfide's lowest percolating barrier is not at least 0.15 eV below the oxide's. Second, for either anion, the framework difference |barrier(A) - barrier(B)| is greater than or equal to the smaller anion-swap difference. A single valid pair is enough to refute; support requires both pairs. A pair counts only under four conditions. (a) All structures use 48-Li-site supercells with one vacancy, and each records its minimum vacancy-image separation. (b) Each rate-limiting hop is repeated at 96 Li sites (256 atoms) and moves by no more than 0.03 eV; otherwise that pair is insufficient data. The larger of the two shifts within a pair is its uncertainty, and a 0.15 eV threshold decision counts only if its margin exceeds that uncertainty. (c) Every symmetry-distinct Li-Li vacancy hop up to 4.0 A is sampled by NEB, and the lowest percolating barrier is scored as the largest climb from any preceding minimum. (d) Substituted structures keep their space group after relaxation, and P stays fourfold-coordinated by X in isolated tetrahedra. An OOD-flagged barrier cannot decide the outcome by itself. If the only valid pair contains an OOD barrier, h2 is logged inconclusive.

batch_plan.strategy: Step 0 records the space group and Z of c-mp-13725 and c-mp-985583. heuristics.text: Before any generation step, write the hypothesis's design as an explicit list of required structures (parent ID plus exact substitution) and give it to the generator; reject any batch containing none of them before it reaches the Skeptic.
Record the space group and Z of every candidate at retrieval; do not label anything 'framework A/B' until both are in the notebook.
Never score a barrier difference between two structures that differ in both anion and framework as evidence for either effect; that diagonal comparison measures neither.
Schedule the Li-metal reaction energy for c-mp-985583 and c-mp-13725 next round, independent of the hypothesis queue; do not report the Pareto frontier as addressing anode stability until it exists.

Gate every forced cross-framework substitution on a relaxation and coordination check before any NEB; if a substituted cell loses its space group or isolated PX4 tetrahedra, log that pair as insufficient data; if both fail, rewrite h2 around frameworks that host both anions natively.
For partial substitutions, record which sites were substituted; on an anion-vs-framework hypothesis, do not propose central-cation swaps.

proposal.title: Closing proposal: Li electrolyte, low barrier, Li-stable
proposal.summary: Nothing was refuted. Both hypotheses closed INCONCLUSIVE, so there are no refutations to lead with. h1 (the anion sets the barrier in Li3PX4) could not be scored: its only pair, c-mp-13725 (Li3PO4) against c-mp-985583 (Li3PS4), failed its own matching rules. Space groups were never recorded, parent cells differ (16 atoms with 2 P against 32 atoms with 4 P), vacancy concentrations differ (1 per 48 Li against 1 per 24 Li), and only one hop was computed per structure. h2 narrowed the claim into a scoreable 2x2 design, then recorded 0 measurements; all four generated candidates (c-h2-4, -6, -7, -8) were correctly vetoed as off-spec, and none of the required pure-anion partners was ever built. Five other candidates were vetoed or never measured, including Li3N (c-mp-2251), a known Li conductor that was off-spec for the PX4 hypotheses and never evaluated. The anode-stability half of the goal has no evidence: the Li-metal reaction energy was scheduled as a standing order after round 1 and again after round 2 and was never computed. What the notebook establishes is narrow. Both parents sit at 0 eV/atom on the Materials Project DFT hull within their own chemical systems (confidence 0.95); c-mp-13725 is experimentally reported, c-mp-985583 is computed-only. MACE-MP-0 reproduces MP GGA energies to within +0.015 eV/atom (oxide) and +0.006 eV/atom (sulfide). Database structures sit close to MACE minima: relaxation drop 0.0015 vs 0.0008 eV/atom, max displacement 0.012 vs 0.014 Å, residual force 0.049 vs 0.028 eV/Å (oxide vs sulfide). One vacancy hop per structure was computed (MACE, confidence 0.60): c-mp-13725 0.326 eV, 2.95 Å hop, 127 atoms, 1 per 48 Li; c-mp-985583 0.275 eV, 3.26 Å hop, 63 atoms, 1 per 24 Li. Not established: any percolating barrier, any barrier uncertainty in eV, whether the 0.051 eV gap is real or a finite-size artefact, whether the two structures share a framework, and any stability ranking (MACE hull 0.0014 vs 0.0092 eV/atom, a 0.0078 eV/atom difference below the 0.015 eV/atom ranking floor). Recommendation: c-mp-985583 (Li3PS4), the only Pareto-frontier member (MACE barrier 0.275 eV, MACE hull 0.0014 eV/atom), only as the candidate to test, with c-mp-13725 (Li3PO4) as matched control; its dominance rests on two unresolved differences and is not established. Before any lab spend, do the cheap computational step scheduled twice and skipped: Li-metal reaction energies for both compounds; space group and Z for both parents; the matched barrier rerun per h2 conditions (a)-(c) — 48-Li one-vacancy cells with c-mp-985583 redone at 128 atoms, every symmetry-distinct hop up to 4.0 Å sampled, rate-limiting hop repeated at 96 Li sites.
synthesis_route: Note: standard literature starting procedures, not outputs of this campaign; phase identity must be confirmed by XRD before any transport or interface measurement counts.
Glovebox handling for all sulfide work under Ar with H2O and O2 below 1 ppm (P2S5 and Li3PS4 hydrolyse in air and release H2S). Precursors Li2S (≥99.9%) and P2S5 (≥99%).
Weigh Li2S:P2S5 = 3:1 molar (3 Li2S + P2S5 → 2 Li3PS4); 2 g batches.

Load into a 45 mL ZrO2 planetary-mill jar with ZrO2 balls at 30:1 ball:powder mass ratio, sealed under Ar. Mill at 370 rpm in 1 h segments with 15 min rests until XRD shows no Li2S reflections; record total milling time.

Split milled powder; seal each aliquot in an evacuated (<10⁻³ mbar) carbon-coated quartz ampoule and anneal 12 h at 150, 250, 350 and 450 °C, 2 °C/min ramps, furnace-cool. The polymorph of mp-985583 is not recorded, so anneal temperature cannot be chosen in advance; take forward only the aliquot whose XRD matches the computed mp-985583 pattern. If none matches, log c-mp-985583 as not synthesised and stop that arm.
Li3PO4 control: mix Li2CO3 and NH4H2PO4 at 3:2 molar (3 Li2CO3 + 2 NH4H2PO4 → 2 Li3PO4 + 3 CO2 + 2 NH3 + 3 H2O); grind in agate mortar 20 min.
Decompose in an alumina crucible in air at 300 °C for 4 h to drive off NH3 and H2O.
Regrind and calcine at 800 °C for 12 h in air. Compare XRD with the computed mp-13725 pattern; if a different Li3PO4 polymorph forms, record which.

Pellets: Li3PS4 cold-pressed at 370 MPa in a PEEK die with stainless-steel plungers inside the glovebox; Li3PO4 uniaxially pressed at 200 MPa then sintered at 900 °C for 6 h in air. Measure geometric density for both. Densification routes differ, so total-conductivity comparisons are confounded by grain boundaries; hence V3 and V4 rely on bulk and local probes.

Li-contact samples: Li|SE|Li symmetric cells with Li foil pressed on both faces at about 10 MPa; separate fragments for XPS contacted with Li foil for 24 h at 25 °C or Li deposited in situ in the XPS chamber. Transfer all samples air-free.
validation_protocol: V0 (computation, before the lab): reaction energy of each phase with Li metal (most negative over decomposition products) on the MP GGA scale; space group and Z for mp-985583 and mp-13725; barrier rerun under h2 conditions (a)-(c) with the 96-Li shift reported as eV uncertainty. Shows whether the frontier ordering survives matched treatment and gives the first measured number on anode stability.

V1 Powder XRD with Rietveld refinement (Cu Kα, or synchrotron if accessible) on every anneal aliquot and the Li3PO4 product: whether product is the computed structure (space group, lattice parameters, Z); weight fraction of crystalline impurities (Li2S, Li4P2S6, Li4P2S7 for sulfide; Li4P2O7 for oxide); for the sulfide, whether site occupancies are partial, meaning mp-985583 is an ordered approximant of a disordered phase.
V2 ³¹P MAS NMR and Raman: whether P is present only as isolated PX4³⁻ tetrahedra or also as P2S7⁴⁻, P2S6⁴⁻ or P2O7⁴⁻ units, including amorphous fractions XRD cannot see.

V3 Variable-temperature ⁷Li NMR spin-lattice relaxation (R1 lab frame and R1ρ, about 150 to 450 K): high-temperature flank gives a local Li hop activation energy with fitted uncertainty; closest to the computed single-hop barrier and least affected by grain boundaries.

V4 Variable-temperature EIS with ion-blocking Au electrodes, 1 MHz to 0.1 Hz, −20 to 80 °C in 10 °C steps: bulk and total conductivity and Arrhenius activation energies, bulk arc fitted separately where resolvable at low temperature. Total activation energy alone is not used to test the barrier because it includes grain-boundary and defect-formation terms.
V5 Li|SE|Li symmetric cells at open circuit, 25 °C, EIS every 2 h for 100 h: whether interfacial area-specific resistance grows, the signature of a continuously forming reduction interphase.

V6 XPS (P 2p, S 2p, O 1s, Li 1s) on pristine and Li-contacted surfaces with Ar⁺ depth profiling: whether Li reduces the electrolyte, via reduced-P (phosphide, Li3P-type) components absent in the pristine reference.
falsification_criteria: F0 Anode stability, computational: 'stays stable against Li metal' is refuted thermodynamically if the V0 reaction energy with Li metal is negative by more than 0.015 eV/atom (the largest MACE–DFT offset seen in this campaign); on a pure DFT calculation the threshold is any negative value. If both candidates fail F0, no candidate from this campaign meets the user's goal.

F1 Phase identity: if no Li3PS4 anneal aliquot indexes to the mp-985583 space group with crystalline impurities ≤5 wt%, c-mp-985583 was not made and every transport and interface result on that sulfide counts neither for nor against the candidate. Same rule for Li3PO4 against mp-13725. If ³¹P NMR shows more than 5% of P outside isolated PX4 units, that sample also fails F1.

F2 Barrier ordering: the claim that c-mp-985583 has a lower barrier than c-mp-13725 is refuted if the matched V0 rerun gives barrier(Li3PS4) ≥ barrier(Li3PO4) − (larger 96-Li shift of the pair), or if on phase-confirmed samples the ⁷Li SLR activation energy of Li3PS4 is at least that of Li3PO4 with 1σ fit intervals not separated in the sulfide's favour. The V0 rerun can only remove the claim, not confirm it; the 0.051 eV gap is not currently resolved.

F3 Absolute barrier: the computed 0.275 eV, presented as an upper bound for the sampled hop, is refuted as such if the ⁷Li SLR activation energy of phase-confirmed Li3PS4 exceeds 0.275 eV by more than twice its fitted standard error. Same test for Li3PO4 at 0.326 eV.

F4 Anode stability, experimental: refuted if XPS after Li contact shows a reduced-P component in P 2p absent from the pristine reference and above 5% of total P 2p area, or if Li|SE|Li area-specific resistance at open circuit rises by more than 50% over 100 h at 25 °C. Either result outranks the band-gap proxy.
caveats: Capability boundary: the atomistic models reach a few hundred atoms over picoseconds. They say nothing about bulk mechanical properties (including the shear modulus relevant to dendrite suppression), long-timescale kinetics, interphase growth or degradation at the Li interface, grain-boundary or microstructural transport (likely dominant for total conductivity in both cold-pressed sulfide and sintered oxide pellets), achievable density, moisture and H2S sensitivity, cell-level performance, cost, or manufacturability. None of those is claimed.

Proxy: energy_above_hull was scored as the 'Stability vs Li metal' objective. It is a within-chemical-system hull distance and cannot speak to reaction with Li metal, so the objective measured the wrong thing for the whole campaign.

Proxy: band_gap (5.818 eV oxide, 2.81 eV sulfide; GGA, confidence 0.60, flagged proxy) stands in for the electrochemical window; it is a lower bound for ordinal use only, and a wide gap does not imply stability against reduction by Li.

Proxy: migration_barrier is a single NEB hop per structure, a proxy for the lowest percolating barrier; it is not a conductivity and ignores defect-formation energy, which enters any measured Arrhenius slope.

MACE hull values (confidence 0.55) are not DFT hull distances and must not be compared with the 0 eV/atom DFT values. 13 phases (oxide system) and 5 phases (sulfide system) larger than 80 atoms were excluded, so either distance may be an underestimate; 3 oxide-system competitors did not converge to fmax 0.05 eV/Å, biasing Li3PO4 toward looking more stable. The 0.0078 eV/atom difference is below the 0.015 eV/atom ranking floor.
OOD flags: no measurement carries one. That is not evidence the model is reliable here, only that it was not flagged.

Not separated: anion effect from framework effect (no anion computed in both frameworks); the 0.051 eV barrier gap from finite-size error (1 vacancy per 48 Li vs 1 per 24 Li, no 96-Li convergence check); whether the two parents share a framework (space groups not recorded; 16-atom vs 32-atom parent cells are a red flag, not proof).

c-mp-985583 is a computed-only phase never reported experimentally and may be an ordered approximant of a partially occupied structure; the synthesis route may not produce it at all, which is why F1 gates every other measurement.
